newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia detains 631 soccer hooligans in capital.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia detains 631 soccer hooligans in capital.

text.p: Indonesian police in the capital Jakarta have detained about 630 soccer hooligans after the penniless fans from the provinces went on a crime spree, the Kompas newspaper reported on Friday.

Jakarta Police Chief Hamami Nata said those detained had been caught stealing food and extorting money after thousands of fans from the provinces came to Jakarta for this weekend's finals of a national soccer tournament.

"You have come to dirty the national capital of this republic. You come with no money and come to cause damage, make trouble and disturb Jakarta's security," Nata was quoted as telling the detainees at police headquarters on Thursday.
"We will take firm action against those who violate the law," he added.

The soccer hooligans were arrested at the three main railway stations at Jatinegara, Senen and Gambir as well as the Senayan stadium in central Jakarta where the National Soccer League finals will take place this weekend.

Most of the fans that have come to Jakarta are from the nation's second largest city, Surabaya. It is an annual tradition for thousands of fans to follow their teams to the capital without paying for their train tickets or carrying sufficient money to live on.
The Jakarta Post daily said the capital's military commander Major-General Sutiyoso has threatened to pack troublemakers into trucks and send them back to Surabaya if they caused problems.

It also quoted National Sports Council chairman Wismoyo Arismunandar as saying he hoped fans would not damage the stadium where the soccer finals are played as it was needed for the Southeast Asia Games in October and organisers had limited funds with which to repair any damage.
